Hi Sanjay / Laura,

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Private VPC deployment with strict egress controls (no control-plane traffic allowed out of your network except approved IPs).
- Air-gapped option for R&D environments for PHI workloads on a per-cluster basis.
- KMS/HSM integration for key control and customer-managed keys.
- On-prem or colocation options for regions where cloud is not acceptable.

How Redwood compares vs hyperscalers (high level)
- Control plane: Redwood Private can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane in VPC, or with a lightweight control-plane proxy that only connects to approved endpoints. Hyperscalers often require persistent outbound egress for telemetry and management which can be a blocker for air-gapped requirements.
- Networking: we support restricted outbound via NAT and allowlisting, and offer an offline install bundle for air-gapped installs. Hyperscalers provide managed services but less flexibility for offline installs.
- Operational tooling: we provide the same Console and observability for Private deployments via an optional private control plane; hyperscalers' managed endpoints tie you to their telemetry and billing models.

Proposed next tests (we recommend running in this order)
1) Networking handshake: confirm required IPs/ports and test connection via a temporary bastion (allowlist exercise).
2) Control plane egress validation: run the proxy mode where control plane calls are restricted to a single egress IP and confirm telemetry buffering behavior.
3) Air-gap smoke install: try the offline bundle in a sandbox R&D cluster (no outbound).
4) Baseline perf test: 100 concurrent chat sessions, 2k token sequences to validate latency and KV-cache behavior on your infra.

Can you confirm which of these you want to run first and target dates? We can bring Marissa (solutions) and Vivek (technical account) to own execution and timelines.

Attachments: redwood_private_networking_checklist.pdf (networking IPs/ports + checklist).

Hi Sanjay / Laura,

Answering your questions and adding a bit more detail for the test plan. High-level: all options outlined by Vanessa are supported; the tradeoffs are the degree of remote telemetry and operational convenience.

1) Control plane telemetry and proxy mode
- In proxy mode the control plane is a lightweight agent that aggregates metrics and state and sends them to Redwood only over an allowlisted outbound IP:443. The agent supports "buffer-and-forward" for short outages and you can set sampling to 0% for non-critical traces. Audit logs (required for SOC-type audits) can be exported to a customer-managed S3-compatible endpoint instead of Redwood's collection service.

2) Offline / air-gapped installer
- We provide a tarball-based offline installer plus a set of container images that can be consumed from a local registry. Installer steps:
  a) Pull images on an internet-connected machine, export to tar bundles.
  b) Transfer tar bundles to the air-gapped environment via secure media.
  c) Run our install script with local registry endpoints and provide KMS/HSM configuration via an offline key injection process.
- Limitations: automatic remote upgrades are not available in fully air-gapped mode; upgrades require a manual bundle install. We document the exact upgrade process in the SOW.

3) Baseline perf test hardware profile
- For a meaningful baseline replicate one of the following (we can target either):
  A) Single-node GPU: NVIDIA A10G / 80GB GPU, 64GB RAM, good for latency-focused tests.
  B) Multi-node modest GPUs: 4x T4s, 128GB aggregate RAM, good for throughput tests.
- We'll provide a perf harness (JMeter-based) and a set of sample prompts and seed data. The perf run we recommend: 100 concurrent sessions, 2k token average, 30-minute sustained window.

Next steps I can take from Redwood side
- Share the networking checklist (attached) with the exact ports and egress IPs.
- Provide the offline bundle instructions and the list of image tags you'll need.
- Schedule a 60-minute networking handshake + test kickoff for the week of Jul 20; please propose two 1-hour slots.

Attachments: redwood_private_networking_checklist.pdf (IP/port matrix + NAT/Proxy checklist).

Hi team, quick note on how Redwood's approach differs from hyperscaler-managed endpoints (to help with procurement conversations):

- Unit economics & billing: Redwood Dedicated/Private separates model serving compute and control-plane services, you can pin model versions and use reserved capacity for predictable unit costs. Hyperscalers often charge per-request with additional telemetry surcharges.

- Routing and fallbacks: our smart routing allows on-prem traffic to be routed to a cheaper compatible model variant or to a dedicated pool in a different region if capacity drops, which preserves SLAs.

- KV cache / latency optimizations: we optimize model runtime (KV cache management, continuous batching) specifically for inference workloads, that tends to reduce token costs relative to naive hosting on general-purpose endpoints.

Proposed quick experiments for differentiation
1) Networking handshake (Marissa to run with you).
2) Offline installer smoke test (air-gap).
3) 1-hour perf window comparing throughput/latency against your current hyperscaler endpoint (we can do 1:1 requests to both and capture traces).

I'll add a short comparison doc to the Drive link and put a proposed SOW draft in DocuSign. Vanessa, can you attach the SOW draft and network diagram we discussed?

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
